issue_title: Fix writing-helper strict acceptance parse error

approach.summary: Fix the release blocker at the PowerShell source-compatibility layer, not in the writing-helper endpoint. Re-save scripts/check-writing-helper.ps1 in a Windows PowerShell-safe encoding, keep its request/assertion semantics intact, and make the regression gate execute the same acceptance path under powershell.exe.
rationale: Explorer evidence shows the failure happens before any HTTP assertion executes in Windows PowerShell, while pwsh reaches the request path.
Existing src-ts/tests/mcp/writing-endpoints.test.ts already covers the writing-helper endpoint contract and local fallback semantics.
The minimal safe fix therefore targets script decoding plus shell-specific regression coverage, not endpoint behavior changes.
non_goals: Do not change POST /writing-helper/process behavior unless the script, once it parses, exposes a separate contract failure.
Do not broaden release-summary or unrelated release-gate logic in this issue.
risk_controls: Use the existing acceptance payloads and strict assertions unchanged so the fix remains isolated to shell compatibility.
Add a regression guard that specifically exercises Windows PowerShell, because pwsh alone cannot catch this class of breakage.

tasks.title: Harden check-writing-helper.ps1 for Windows PowerShell decoding
tasks.description: Re-save scripts/check-writing-helper.ps1 as UTF-8 with BOM and keep the current request bodies, strict assertions, and output contract unchanged. If a warning comment is added, keep it ASCII-only and limited to editor/encoding guidance.
acceptance: powershell.exe can parse the script without mojibake/parser failure.
The script still posts to /writing-helper/process with the same cases and strict checks.

tasks.title: Run the blocking acceptance path under Windows PowerShell in release wiring
tasks.description: Update the reusable writing-helper acceptance workflow to invoke the script through Windows PowerShell instead of relying only on pwsh. Align docs/release/SIGN_OFF.md with the exact powershell.exe invocation used for release proof so local and CI sign-off follow the same shell path.
acceptance: The blocking CI/local release path uses powershell.exe for check-writing-helper execution.
Gateway startup, failed-case artifact upload, and cleanup behavior remain unchanged.

tasks.title: Pin the shell contract in existing regression tests
tasks.description: Extend the existing governance/script regression surface to verify the sign-off and workflow shell contract for writing-helper acceptance, and add a lightweight byte-level assertion that scripts/check-writing-helper.ps1 keeps the required UTF-8 BOM. Reuse tests/unit/scripts/test_governance_scripts.py rather than creating a new harness.
acceptance: A targeted automated test fails if the workflow/docs drift away from the Windows PowerShell execution path.
A targeted automated test fails if scripts/check-writing-helper.ps1 loses the BOM required for Windows PowerShell compatibility.

dependencies: Windows PowerShell 5.1 BOM-sensitive decoding of UTF-8 source files containing non-ASCII literals.
Existing writing-helper endpoint contract covered by src-ts/tests/mcp/writing-endpoints.test.ts.
Release sign-off flow documented in docs/release/SIGN_OFF.md and enforced through .github/workflows/writing-helper-acceptance.yml.
validation_commands: npm --prefix src-ts exec -- vitest run tests/mcp/writing-endpoints.test.ts --reporter=default
